name: example-engine
purpose: Own deterministic admission and lifecycle decisions for reusable work units.

fit_evidence: Both adapters share stable admission semantics.
Durable recovery and one reservation authority are required.

boundary.mechanism: Validate commands, commit facts, and request post-commit effects
non_goals: Calling external systems inside the reducer
boundary.state_authority: One engine aggregate is the single writer per work-unit id

state_model: A versioned Job lifecycle FSM validated with $fsm-design.

protocol.versioning: Additive fields are backward compatible; breaking changes require a new major schema.

invariants: A terminal job cannot return to a running state.

runtime.ordering: Commands are serialized per job id.
runtime.concurrency: Different job ids may progress concurrently.
runtime.backpressure: Reject admission with retry guidance when the bounded queue is full.
runtime.cancellation: Cancellation is a command and produces an auditable terminal event.
runtime.timeouts: External waits have typed deadlines and timeout events.

durability.persistence: Append accepted domain events before exposing success.
durability.atomic_commit: Commit dedup claim, expected-version events, snapshot pointer, and outbox intents atomically.
durability.recovery: Rebuild state by replay, then resume unacknowledged outbox effects.
durability.effect_idempotency: Use event id plus effect index as the idempotency key.
durability.migration: Upcast old event versions during replay; retain original bytes.

failure_model: Invalid commands are rejected without mutation.
Transient port failures exhaust into an observable state.

traces: Command, decision, committed event, and effect attempt share correlation and causation ids.
metrics: Queue depth, rejection, version conflict, outbox lag, recovery duration, and effect failure counts.
observability.redaction: Security-domain identifiers stay in protected traces and never become high-cardinality metric labels.

security: Private-domain traffic cannot alter shared decisions.
verification: Crash-test every cut point around commit and effect acknowledgement.
implementation_slices: One consumer, SubmitJob, JobSubmitted, the event store, and one crash recovery path.
falsifiers: If shared state authority and durability disappear, collapse this into a pure module.
